narrative.overview:
Periscope is the category-standard monitoring console, played straight and finished to the bar of Linear, Vercel, Grafana and Waymo-style perception views. Near-black panels carry the instruments: the floor camera with its calibrated wedge and a camera/shadow wipe, a plan-view corner map with a protractor, a spacetime strip, the alert, the agent's reasoning and the scores. Every view runs on the same clock, so any warning can be followed back to the shadow on the floor that caused it. The interface's job is to make a 0.3% change in floor brightness readable and believable, from a judge's distance, without anyone touching it: the run starts on its own and loops.

The system is dense but quiet. Panels sit edge to edge on a 16px gap and are separated by hairlines. Data sits in recessed wells. Type is steady and never smaller than 12px, and colour carries meaning instead of decoration. The only loud thing on the page is STOP. When someone is coming, the alert card and the header status pill go solid red and the word STOP appears at poster size. It is the single moment the console raises its voice. Indigo is Periscope's own ink, for whatever the system drew or computed. Green, amber and red describe the corner and nothing else. Geist Mono, with tabular figures, appears only where a number is a measurement.

The secondary tool pages (calibration) use the same tokens with fewer parts: the panel recipe without the gradient, the same segmented control, buttons and wells. A new surface should look like another panel in the same console, not like a separate site.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only (`color-scheme: dark`), on a cool blue-black neutral ramp.
Hairline borders (1px) do the structural work; there is almost no shadow.
Recessed wells hold every video, canvas, map and diagram.
One indigo system accent, plus a three-colour state triad reserved for corner state.
One sanctioned solid fill: STOP red, on the alert card and the status pill, only while someone is coming.
Geist for language, Geist Mono for measurements; a 12px legibility floor.
Motion only on state change and playback; reduced motion turns it all off, including autoplay.

rules.name: The Reserved Triad Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean corner state (clear, present, coming) and nothing else: no branding, no decorative tints, no category colours. If a colour has to say something that isn't corner state, it is indigo or a neutral.

rules.name: The System Ink Rule
rules.body: Indigo marks what Periscope itself measured or drew: the wedge, the corner, the protractor, the bearing, the track. When the alarm fires, the bearing switches from lilac (or white on camera) to Alarm Red. It does not get a third colour.

rules.name: The Washes, Not Fills Rule
rules.body: A state colour fills an area only as a low-alpha wash (10–32%: the present alert card, the plan's bearing cone, the "in view" zone). Full-strength state colour is kept for dots, rays, arcs, borders and traces. STOP is the single sanctioned exception: in the coming state, and only then, the alert card and the header status pill fill solid Stop Red with white text. No other surface, state or component takes a solid state fill.

rules.name: The Measurement Mono Rule
rules.body: If a string is a measurement (bearing, seconds, σ, metres, pixel coordinates), set it in Geist Mono with `tabular-nums` so values hold still while they update. Words stay in Geist, including words inside a mono-heavy panel.

rules.name: The Small Unit Rule
rules.body: A unit sits beside its number, smaller (14px next to a 26px readout) and in Quiet Grey. The number carries the weight.

rules.name: The Legibility Floor Rule
rules.body: No text is set below 12px, in HTML or canvas. Anything a judge must read from a distance (alert text, readouts, panel titles, the status) sits at 14–16px or larger. Labels at 12–13px use Quiet Grey or brighter, never a dimmer tone.

rules.name: The One Clock Rule
rules.body: Every view registers to one frame index: both floor videos and the overlay, the plan's bearing and protractor, the spacetime cursor, the shadow-strength cursor, the alert readouts and the decision log (future entries fade to 42%). Any new view of run data takes its time from the same cursor and scrubs with it.

rules.name: The Wedge-First Rule
rules.body: The floor camera is the largest panel and reads first, because it holds the evidence. Derived views (map, spacetime, scores) are always smaller and placed after it.

rules.name: The Kiosk Rule
rules.body: The console plays itself. A run autoplays on load and loops 2.5s after it ends, until someone pauses it. Autoplay is off under `prefers-reduced-motion` and with `?autoplay=0`; a user pause always wins.

rules.name: The Wells Sink Rule
rules.body: Anything that shows signal (video, canvas, plan, diagram, coordinate field) sits in a well darker than its panel. Panels rise slightly and data sinks. Panels never nest inside panels.

rules.name: The State-Only Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion marks state changes and playback. Transitions run 150–350ms on `cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)`. Entering STOP plays a 0.6s scale settle (0.985 → 1.012 → 1) once. The 1s white ping loops only while someone is coming, and the HUD recording dot blinks only while the run is playing. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes all animation and transitions.

rules.name: The Truth Is Dashed Rule
rules.body: Ground truth and thresholds draw dashed at reduced opacity (the true-position ring on the plan, the truth trace, the 4.9σ line, the calibrated angle rays). Periscope's own estimate draws solid. A reader always knows which line is the camera and which is the referee.

dos: Do put every video, canvas, map and diagram in a well with a 1px border and a 10px radius, inset 12px inside its panel.
Do set every measurement in Geist Mono with tabular figures, with its unit smaller and in Quiet Grey beside it.
Do give each panel a Title-scale heading plus a one-line Quiet Grey caption saying what the view shows.
Do keep text at 12px or larger, and judge-critical text (alert, readouts, titles, status) at 14–16px or larger.
Do draw ground truth and thresholds dashed and Periscope's estimate solid.
Do tie every new run-data view to the shared time cursor, so scrubbing one scrubs all.
Do put a legend under any panel that draws keyed marks, with a swatch for each.
Do label synthetic runs with the synthetic tag or in the run name.
Do keep one primary (Wedge Indigo) button per surface.
Do keep autoplay off under reduced motion and when `?autoplay=0` is set.
donts: Don't use green, amber or red for anything but corner state: no decorative glows, category colours or brand moments in the triad.
Don't fill a surface with solid state colour anywhere except the STOP alert card and the STOP status pill. Every other state surface is a wash at 32% or less.
Don't put text on the STOP fill in anything but white or near-white, and don't set it below 14px.
Don't set measurements in proportional Geist, or set prose in Geist Mono.
Don't nest a panel inside a panel. Inner structure is wells, hairlines and dashed rows.
Don't animate anything that isn't a state change or playback, and don't loop motion outside the coming state and a playing run.
Don't introduce a light theme or a second accent hue. The console is dark-only with one system voice; Tape Blue keys a physical material, not a UI accent.
